name: Fairmont Miramar Hotel & Bungalows
positioning: Fairmont Miramar Hotel & Bungalows, a Santa Monica resort with private bungalows on five acres atop the bluffs above the beaches
best_for: Travelers who want a garden bungalow stay on the Santa Monica bluffs

facts.text: The resort has private bungalows set on five acres atop the bluffs above Santa Monica's beaches.
The resort was born from a grand 19th-century estate.
The Palisades Wing was built in the 1920s and its rooms feel more traditional.
Suites in the Palisades Building have record players.
Soko is the resort's sushi venue.
FIG's menu uses local and organic ingredients from the nearby Santa Monica Farmer's Market.
Guests can have a massage by the pool or in their room.
The indoor-outdoor fitness center is open 24 hours and has ocean views.
The property is very dog friendly.
The pool and Jacuzzi are heated.

highlights.text: The bungalows are residential-style and sit in the flower-filled Miramar Gardens.
A large Moreton Bay Fig tree at the entrance predates the 100-year-old property.
Top-floor suites in the Ocean Tower have two furnished balconies overlooking the beach.
The Bungalow bar has a deck with an outdoor firepit, a billiard room and a back garden.
EMWell Spa offers massages, facials and body rituals using ocean-inspired ingredients.

considerations.text: Basic Wi-Fi is included in the daily resort fee, so a resort fee applies.
There is no complimentary shuttle between the hotel and the airport.
Parking is available for an additional fee, with valet service.

sources.title: Condé Nast Traveler: Fairmont Miramar Hotel & Bungalows
